entity.name: Black Mirror
entity.description: Black Mirror, created by Charlie Brooker and first released in 2011, is a British anthology television series that presents standalone near-future dramas exploring the societal and personal costs of technology. Each episode functions as a self-contained film combining elements of drama, science fiction, mystery and thriller, and frequently uses satire and moral irony to interrogate themes such as surveillance, social media, privacy and human frailty. The series features a rotating cast across episodes, including performers such as Anjana Vasan, Cristin Milioti and Jimmi Simpson, and is notable for its unsettling atmosphere and thought-provoking twists. Overall, the show aims to provoke reflection and unease about plausible technological developments and their ethical consequences.

entity.name: Money Heist
entity.description: Money Heist (original Spanish title La Casa de Papel) is a 2017 crime-thriller television series created by Álex Pina. Centered on a master planner who recruits a ragtag team of thieves identified by city codenames, the series chronicles an elaborate takeover of Spain's Royal Mint and its aftermath. With a large ensemble cast led by Álvaro Morte and Úrsula Corberó alongside Itziar Ituño, Pedro Alonso, Alba Flores, Miguel Herrán and others, the show blends pulse-pounding heist mechanics with intimate character backstories, romance, and ideological conflict. Visually bold and fast-paced, the series explores themes of class struggle, loyalty, identity, media spectacle and the ethics of resistance while maintaining a tense, emotionally charged tone that balances spectacle and character-driven drama.

entity.name: For Life
entity.description: For Life (2020) is an American crime and legal drama created by Hank Steinberg and inspired by the true story of Isaac Wright Jr. It stars Nicholas Pinnock as Aaron Wallace, a man wrongfully convicted who becomes a practicing lawyer while serving a life sentence, and features a supporting ensemble that brings the prison and courtroom worlds to life. Across its episodes, and directed by a team of television directors, the series blends courtroom procedure, serialized character arcs, and prison-set drama to chronicle Wallace’s efforts to overturn his conviction and to represent fellow inmates. The narrative explores systemic corruption, the moral complexities of legal advocacy, and the personal costs of incarceration, delivering a tense, emotionally charged tone that balances harrowing setbacks with moments of hard-won redemption.

entity.name: Stateless
entity.description: Stateless (2020) is an Australian dramatic miniseries directed by Emma Freeman and Jocelyn Moorhouse that dramatizes the intersecting lives of four people detained at a remote immigration facility. Through a grounded, character-focused narrative it explores themes of identity, displacement, bureaucratic injustice and mental-health strain, drawing inspiration from real-world events surrounding unlawful detention. The series blends political and social-issue drama conventions with a gritty, emotionally raw style to deliver an intimate, morally urgent portrait of confinement, connection and the human cost of immigration policy.

entity.name: Hunters
entity.description: Hunters (2020) is a 1970s-set crime drama created by David Weil that blends mystery, conspiracy thriller, and vigilante themes. Starring Al Pacino, Logan Lerman and Lena Olin, the series follows a covert group hunting high-ranking Nazis in hiding while interrogating survivor trauma and moral compromise. It intercuts brutal action and comic-book–influenced visuals with flashbacks to Holocaust-era atrocities, producing a tense, emotionally provocative tone. The show pairs glossy, stylized direction with a dark, morally ambiguous narrative about justice and revenge.
